```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This notebook calculates WSS (Weighted Sum of Scores) module scores for
your cohort two ways, using the `WSSmod` package
(<https://github.com/Longo-Lab/WSSmod>):

1. **Actual** scores, computed directly from your proteomic panel via
   `WSSmod::calculate_WSS()`.
2. **Predicted** scores, computed from just Age, Gender, and the 8 core
   plasma biomarkers via `WSSmod::predict_WSS()` — no proteomic panel
   required for this half.

It then merges your (probe-level) proteomics with both sets of WSS scores
and your clinical/demographic data into one intermediate file,
`dataProt_replication.csv.gz`. This file is deliberately **not** filtered
or covariate-selected yet — that happens next, in `02-sample_QC_prediction.R`
(see this folder's `README.md` for the full run order).

Install `WSSmod` first if you haven't already:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Longo-Lab/WSSmod")
```

## Required input files

Edit the `params` block at the top of this Rmd (or pass them via
`rmarkdown::render(params = list(...))`) to point at your own data:

- **`proteomics_path`** — CSV, one row per sample. First column
  `SampleID`. Remaining columns are protein levels. By default these are
  expected to be **SomaLogic probe IDs**, either as probe names
  (e.g. `CRYBB2.10000.28.3`) or as SeqIds (e.g. `seq.10000.28`), matching
  the bundled `soma_probe_to_symbol_key.csv` — if your panel doesn't cover
  every probe in the key that's fine, but any collaborator probe ID not
  found there is a data problem worth checking. If your proteomics matrix
  is already gene-symbol-named (e.g. a non-SomaScan platform), set
  `map_probes_to_symbols: FALSE` in `params`. Supply the protein levels on
  their usual (normalized RFU) scale, not log-transformed or scaled; the
  notebook rank-normalizes them before scoring (see Step 1).
- **`biomarker_path`** — CSV, one row per sample. Columns: `SampleID`,
  `Age`, `Gender` (1 = male, 0 = not male), and the 8 **raw** (not
  normalized) core plasma biomarkers: `PlasmaPTau181`, `PlasmaAB142P`,
  `PlasmaAB140P`, `PlasmaABRatio`, `PlasmapTau217`,
  `PlasmapTau217_AB42Ratio`, `PlasmaGFAP`, `PlasmaNfL`.
- **`clinical_path`** — CSV, one row per sample. Columns: `SampleID`,
  `Age`, `Gender`, `CognitiveScore` (MoCA or equivalent, continuous), and
  `Diagnosis_bin` (0 = control, 1 = case/impaired), plus any other
  demographic/technical variables you recorded (see the "Choosing
  covariates" section of `README.md` — Age/Gender are only a starting
  point).

The following are **bundled platform/curation reference files already in
this folder** — you don't need to generate or edit them:
`2024-08-30_Somalogic_reference_Key.txt`, `prot_names.txt`,
`WSS_names.txt`, `WSS_names_pred.txt`, `soma_probe_to_symbol_key.csv`.

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(WSSmod)
  library(data.table)
  library(RNOmni)
})
```

## Step 1: Load proteomics, map probes to gene symbols, normalize

`WSSmod::calculate_WSS()` needs a gene-symbol-named expression matrix,
but your raw proteomics is (by default) SomaLogic-probe-named. This step
builds a symbol-named matrix for `calculate_WSS()` while keeping the
original probe-level table intact for the full-panel association tests
in `00-commands.sh`.

`calculate_WSS()` does no scaling of its own, and the bundled module
weights were built on a rank-based inverse normal (INT) scale. Each protein
is therefore rank-normalized across your samples
(`normalize_proteomics: TRUE`, the default). Scoring raw RFU instead lets
the highest-abundance proteins dominate every module score.

```{r load_proteomics}
prot_dt <- fread(params$proteomics_path)
sample_ids <- prot_dt$SampleID

if (isTRUE(params$map_probes_to_symbols)) {
  key <- fread(params$probe_symbol_key_path)

  # columns are either probe names (CRYBB2.10000.28.3) or SeqIds (seq.10000.28)
  id_col <- if (any(startsWith(names(prot_dt), "seq."))) "seq" else "ix"

  missing_probes <- setdiff(key[[id_col]], names(prot_dt))
  if (length(missing_probes) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Note: %d of %d key probes not found in your proteomics matrix (ok if your panel doesn't cover them)\n",
      length(missing_probes), nrow(key)
    ))
  }

  # join each probe's values onto every symbol it resolves to -- this
  # naturally duplicates a multi-gene "complex" probe's values across
  # each constituent gene's column
  present_key <- key[get(id_col) %in% names(prot_dt)]
  stopifnot("no key probes found in the proteomics matrix" = nrow(present_key) > 0)
  probe_cols <- present_key[[id_col]]
  probe_matrix <- as.matrix(prot_dt[, ..probe_cols])
  colnames(probe_matrix) <- present_key$Symbol
  rownames(probe_matrix) <- sample_ids
  expr_matrix <- probe_matrix
} else {
  expr_matrix <- as.matrix(prot_dt[, -"SampleID"])
  rownames(expr_matrix) <- sample_ids
}

if (isTRUE(params$normalize_proteomics)) {
  # rank-based inverse normal transform of each protein across samples
  expr_matrix <- apply(expr_matrix, 2, RNOmni::RankNorm)
  rownames(expr_matrix) <- sample_ids
}
```

## Step 2: Actual WSS scores from proteomics

```{r calculate_wss}
# uses the bundled core_AD_plasma_biomarkers STRING module/weighting table
wss_actual <- WSSmod::calculate_WSS(expr_matrix)

actual_scores <- as.data.table(wss_actual$scores, keep.rownames = "SampleID")
```

## Step 3: Predicted WSS scores from biomarkers + Age/Gender

```{r predict_wss}
biomarker_dt <- fread(params$biomarker_path)

raw_biomarkers <- biomarker_dt[, .(
  PlasmaPTau181, PlasmaAB142P, PlasmaAB140P, PlasmaABRatio,
  PlasmapTau217, PlasmapTau217_AB42Ratio, PlasmaGFAP, PlasmaNfL
)]

# method = "project" (default) is safe for any cohort size, including a
# single new patient -- it scores each value against the bundled
# baseline reference distribution rather than the collaborator's own
# cohort, avoiding leakage/re-fitting concerns
normalized <- WSSmod::normalize_wss_biomarkers(raw_biomarkers, method = "project")

newdata <- cbind(
  Age = biomarker_dt$Age,
  Gender = biomarker_dt$Gender,
  normalized
)

pred <- WSSmod::predict_WSS(newdata)

predicted_scores <- as.data.table(pred$meta)
predicted_scores[, SampleID := biomarker_dt$SampleID]
setcolorder(predicted_scores, "SampleID")
# suffix predicted module columns with .pred to match the actual-vs-predicted
# naming convention used throughout the rest of the pipeline
setnames(predicted_scores, setdiff(names(predicted_scores), "SampleID"),
  paste0(setdiff(names(predicted_scores), "SampleID"), ".pred"))
```

## Step 4: Merge probe-level proteomics + WSS scores + clinical data

```{r merge}
clinical_dt <- fread(params$clinical_path)

merged <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "SampleID"),
  list(prot_dt, actual_scores, predicted_scores, clinical_dt))
```

## Step 5: Write the intermediate file

This is deliberately the **raw merge only** — no covariate selection or
filtering happens here. That's the job of `02-sample_QC_prediction.R`,
run manually next (see `README.md`).

```{r write_outputs}
dir.create(params$output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

fwrite(merged,
  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "dataProt_replication.csv.gz")
)

cat(sprintf(
  "Wrote %d samples x %d proteins, %d actual + %d predicted WSS modules\n",
  nrow(merged),
  ncol(prot_dt) - 1,
  ncol(actual_scores) - 1,
  ncol(predicted_scores) - 1
))
```

Next: run `02-sample_QC_prediction.R` (see `README.md`) to choose
covariates/surrogate variables per outcome, then `00-commands.sh` to
reproduce the Figure 6 association analyses, then
`05-Figure6_comparison.Rmd` to compare the actual-vs-predicted results.
